_note: Every scheme carries a `sourced` flag and a `source` string. `sourced: true` means the colours trace to a specific plate in Camo Specs (FASA, 1988), whose citations came with the previous version of this page. `sourced: false` means the colours are an interpretation from general canon and have NOT been checked against a sourcebook — the page says so on the card. Correct anything wrong here and the page picks it up; no code to touch.
_caveat: Camo Specs is 1988 and predates the Clans entirely: its 44 plates are all Inner Sphere and mercenary regiments. No Clan scheme in this file is sourced from it.
_roles: primary = the bulk of the armour. secondary = the contrast panels, usually limbs or torsos. accent = trim, stripes, unit markings. cockpit = the canopy glass, used by the gemming step.

schemes.notes: The Combine's household regiments, and the most recognisable red in the Inner Sphere. Black trim does the separating, and the gold dragon goes on the centre torso or the left shoulder. A red this saturated needs a warm undercoat or it goes pink over grey plastic.
Blue-grey over near-white, with a red stripe doing the work. The white reads better as a very light warm grey than as pure white; keep actual white for the stripe edges and stencils.

schemes.source: Camo Specs (FASA, 1988), plates 22 — Wolverine and 44 — Manticore
schemes.notes: Ice blue with white and gold. The palest Lyran schemes are the hardest to keep clean-looking: shade the recesses only, and leave the flat panels alone.

schemes.source: Camo Specs (FASA, 1988), plates 25 — Catapult and 31 — Marauder
schemes.notes: Deep green with white trim. A green this dark swallows a black wash, so shade with a brown-green and put the contrast in the highlight instead.
The Liao household regiment, and red rather than the green most Capellan units wear. Worth knowing if you were about to paint a whole Capellan force green.

schemes.source: Camo Specs (FASA, 1988), plates 7 — Stinger and 28 — Thunderbolt
schemes.notes: Two purples rather than a purple and a neutral, which is what makes the League look like the League. Purple over grey plastic goes muddy — undercoat white or use a light grey.

schemes.source: Camo Specs (FASA, 1988), plate 30 — Natasha Kerensky's Warhammer
schemes.notes: Black with a bone secondary and the red spider. Flat black kills all detail: base with a very dark grey instead and save true black for the panel lines.

schemes.notes: White and grey with red trim. The classic problem scheme: white over dark plastic needs three thin coats, or a white primer and a grey shade to bring the panels back.

schemes.notes: Grey with a red chevron and black weapon housings. The most forgiving Clan scheme to paint: the grey does the work and the chevron is the only fiddly part.

schemes.notes: Dark navy over a cream secondary. The cream wants to be off-white and slightly warm, not bone and not white, or it fights the navy.

schemes.notes: Near-black with orange-red spotting. Do the spots last, thinned, and irregularly — evenly spaced spots read as polka dots at tabletop distance.

schemes.notes: Deep navy with a gold secondary and white trim. Three strong colours, so keep the gold to panels rather than edges or it overwhelms the navy.

schemes.notes: Black over red. Reads as a merc unit rather than a House one because there is no trim colour doing the tidying — the two blocks just meet.
